draft.title: Surrogacy and birth technologies
card: Surrogacy
A woman agrees to carry and give birth to a child for another person or couple, who intend to raise the child. The people who will raise the child are called the intended parents.
Altruistic
The surrogate is not paid for carrying the child. Her reasonable medical and related costs may be covered. This kind of surrogacy is legal in NSW.
Commercial
The surrogate is paid for carrying the child, beyond her reasonable costs. Under NSW law, this is a crime.
Birth technologies, such as IVF, have outpaced the law. The law is still working out the rights of everyone involved: the child, the surrogate and the intended parents.
draft.remember: NSW allows unpaid surrogacy and makes paid surrogacy a crime, while the law on everyone's rights is still developing.

a.q: Priya agrees to carry a child for her cousin and his partner. She is paid only for her reasonable medical costs. How does NSW law treat this?
opts: It is legal altruistic surrogacy
It is a crime because money was involved
It is illegal because the parties are related
It is legal only if she is paid a fee
a.why: Priya receives no payment beyond reasonable costs, so this is altruistic surrogacy, which is legal in NSW. Covering costs is not the same as being paid for carrying the child, so the option about money is wrong.
a.clue: Look at what kind of payment she receives.

b.q: Dan and Lee, a couple in Newcastle, offer a woman a large fee to carry their child, and she agrees. Which statement best describes the law in NSW?
opts: The arrangement is paid surrogacy, which is a crime
The arrangement is altruistic, so it is legal
The arrangement is legal because both parties agreed
The law has settled every right of the child already
b.why: A fee beyond reasonable costs makes this paid surrogacy, which is a crime in NSW. Agreement between the parties does not make it legal. The law on the rights of everyone involved is still developing, so the last option is also wrong.
b.clue: Consent does not decide whether a payment is lawful.

b.best: The arrangement is paid surrogacy, which is a crime

problems.detail: Why (b) calls 'The law has settled every right of the child already' 'the last option'. Options are shown in random order, and here it appears first, so a student reading the explanation could be confused. Name the option by its content instead.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate for NSW (Surrogacy Act 2010), and each question has one clear right answer. The only problem is that Why (b) refers to an option by position ('the last option'), which does not hold when options are shuffled.
